chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jab-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
Regarding the child testifying to the testimony, he said: 'If he understands it when he reaches maturity, that he is telling the truth, his testimony is valid.'
ai.seo_question: Under what conditions is a child's testimony considered valid in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential criterion for the validity of a child's testimony, linking it to the attainment of 'aql (intellect) and the capacity to discern truth. In Shia legal theory, this establishes that the key factor is not merely chronological age, but the cognitive maturity required to understand the gravity of the statement, ensuring the testimony is reliable and legally binding.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>)
having said regarding the child testifying upon the witnessing, said: ‘If his intellect as become aware that it is true, his testimony is allowed’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Muhammad ibn Humran who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the testimony of children.
He (the Imam) said, ‘No, except in the case of murder, in which case his first words are accepted but his second words are not accepted.’”
